intro.title: Default Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Vue component that displays user profile information. You'll learn how to use default props to provide fallback values when parent components don't pass specific data. The core concept is component communication through props with safety nets for missing data. You'll work with Vue's props system, JavaScript objects, and the defineProps compiler macro. This will help you create more robust components that handle missing data gracefully.
intro.usecase: Default props are essential for creating reusable components that work reliably even when parent components don't provide all expected data. In real-world Vue applications, you'll see this pattern in dashboard widgets that need sensible fallback values when data isn't available, form input components that should display placeholder text when no label is provided, and UI card components that need default styling when no custom classes are passed. This ensures your components never break unexpectedly and provide consistent user experiences across different parts of your application.
